The planting shades the roof surface, and vegetation cools surrounding air through evapotranspiration, mitigating the urban heat island effect. Green roofs provide thermal mass and natural insulation, stabilizing indoor temperatures, so green roofs improve energy efficiency, reduce energy consumption by improving insulation, and can save on energy costs over time for the floors below.

extend past the building to the environment. sections.heading: What Are the Disadvantages of Green Roofs?

sections.heading: Green Roof Permits, New Jersey Stormwater Rules, and the 25% Rule

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: It has two meanings. As a rule of thumb, once damage covers about a quarter of a roof, replacement usually costs less over time than repeated repairs; and under the New Jersey Uniform Construction Code, repairing more than 25% of a commercial, multi-family, or attached building's roof area within 12 months requires a construction permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. New Jersey's Uniform Construction Code mandates permits for roofing alterations beyond ordinary maintenance, and a green roof installation on those buildings is new construction work on the roof, so plan for the permit.
